shouldFix.title: The V7-A2 repair adds a second open-decision registry, /openDecisions, alongside the existing /namedOpenDecisions, with no cross-reference and a divergent id convention
detail: /openDecisions is the only new top-level key in v8: [{id: OD-V8-1, finding: [CLAUDE-V6-A2, CLAUDE-V6-A3], decision: ..., standing: 'OPEN. Not folded at v8.', owner: 'this schema surface (DR-103)', doesNotBlockLockDeferral: ...}].

/namedOpenDecisions already exists, byte-identical from v2 through v8, and carries OD-1 (the size-caps question) with the shape {id, decision, standing, candidateOwners, consequence}. The two entries model the same thing - an open decision on this surface with an owner and a stated consequence - in two containers whose names differ only by the word 'named'.
Neither container references the other: /namedOpenDecisions does not mention OD-V8-1 and /openDecisions does not mention OD-1. I checked both strings directly.
The id conventions diverge: OD-1 in the old container, OD-V8-1 in the new one.

This matters beyond tidiness because the register tracks the old container by name. The live SRC-08 DR-103 row states that 'named open decision OD-1 ... remains OPEN with its owner UNASSIGNED'. A reader following the register into /namedOpenDecisions to enumerate this surface's open decisions will not find OD-V8-1.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: My V7-A2 was specifically about findability: the carried CLAUDE-V6-A2/A3 could 'only be recovered by reading this successor's prose', and the remedy I offered was 'naming the owning surface, or recording them as a named open decision the way OD-1 already models'. v8 does name the owner, which is real progress. But by recording the decision in a new parallel container rather than the one OD-1 models, it substitutes one findability problem for another: the decision is now in a structure that nothing else in the artifact, and nothing in the register, points at.
shouldFix.steelman: A deliberate split is conceivable - /namedOpenDecisions for design questions the schema declines to settle, /openDecisions for review findings carried forward. If that is the intent it is defensible, but nothing in v8 states it, the two entry shapes are near-identical, and the names do not signal the distinction.
shouldFix.remedy: Move OD-V8-1 into /namedOpenDecisions with an id in that container's convention, or - if the split is intentional - state the distinction at both containers and cross-reference them, so enumerating this surface's open decisions is a single lookup.

repairVerification.finding: V7-B1 (Codex blocker) - three v6-to-v7 source paths changed outside the v7 repairLog
repairVerification.disposition: REPAIRED - VERIFIED, to the extent a successor can repair it
repairVerification.howIChecked: The v7 delta is frozen history and cannot be re-accounted from v8; what a successor can do is stop repeating the pattern and make its own delta complete. v8 does both. /sources/reMeasurementAtV8 is added by an explicit named operation under V7-B1 - the exact treatment Codex's requiredRepair asked for ('Treat reMeasurementAtV7 as authoring metadata with its own named ADD operation'), applied to v8's own custody key. /sources/reMeasurementAtV7 is left byte-identical, which I confirmed, and v8 states that it is left so as a historical v7 authoring note. Most importantly the completeness claim now holds: I mapped all 23 v7-to-v8 diff sites and every one is named by V7-B1, V7-S1, V7-A1, V7-A2 or META-v8. That is the property Codex's blocker was about, restored at 23-for-23.
repairVerification.residual: See advisory V8-A2 on one sentence in the V7-S1 entry that overstates what this accounting achieves.

repairVerification.finding: V7-S1 (Claude SHOULD-FIX) - three /sources paths changed without any repairLog operation naming them
repairVerification.howIChecked: Same underlying defect as Codex's V7-B1, and v8 splits the response across two entries rather than merging them, which keeps each reviewer's finding traceable. The two historical reference paths I named, /sources/reMeasurementAtV2 and /sources/reMeasurementAtV5, are now each named by an explicit AMEND operation, and the entry states that they are 'updated for field-name resolution only'. My finding's second aspect was that mutating historical notes 'is a choice that should be stated, not made silently' - v8 states it. Both notes' measured values are unchanged: reMeasurementAtV2 still carries the v2 head and the v1 head a2ad75d0..., reMeasurementAtV5 still carries its v5-era scoping.
repairVerification.residual: See advisory V8-A1 on the redundancy of the appended clauses.

repairVerification.finding: V7-A2 (Claude advisory) - the carry reason routed a schema-shape decision to a corpus milestone without naming an owning row
repairVerification.disposition: REPAIRED IN SUBSTANCE - the owner is now named; see V8-S1 on where it was recorded
repairVerification.howIChecked: notFoldedThisSuccessor is rewritten to drop the unowned milestone routing. Where v7 said normalization 'may [happen] after SATISFIED-GRADE corpus review', v8 says 'Owner: this schema surface (DR-103). Activation: a later successor of this artifact, not a SATISFIED-GRADE corpus review by itself.' That directly answers the advisory - the work now has a named owner and an activation condition tied to a surface rather than to someone else's milestone. The accompanying OD-V8-1 entry gives it an id and a standing. My finding is answered; the container it was recorded in is a new issue, raised as V8-S1.

advisories.title: The clauses appended to reMeasurementAtV2 and reMeasurementAtV5 restate what those notes already said, and mutate historical records a second time
advisories.detail: v7 had already rewritten both notes to use corpusHeadAtV2Authoring - that silent rewrite was the defect Codex and I both reported. v8 now appends to each: 'v8 name-resolution only: the live field name is corpusHeadAtV2Authoring...'. Both notes already named corpusHeadAtV2Authoring before this append, so the new clauses add no information a reader lacked. The effect is that two historical measurement notes have now been edited in two consecutive successors, in the same revision where v8 states the opposite principle for a sibling: 'The v7 key /sources/reMeasurementAtV7 is left byte-identical (historical v7 authoring note).' A repairLog note recording that v7's edit is accepted as history, with no further mutation, would have satisfied both verdicts without touching the notes again.
advisories.notBlocking: The operations are named, so the completeness property holds, and nothing added is false. The measured values in both notes are unchanged.

advisories.title: One sentence in the V7-S1 entry asserts an accounting relationship that does not hold
advisories.detail: The entry closes: 'The v7 ADD of reMeasurementAtV7 remains historical and is now accounted by V7-B1's ADD of reMeasurementAtV8.' Adding a new key in v8 does not account for an unnamed addition made in v7 - those are different paths in different deltas, and v7's repairLog is frozen. The true and sufficient statement is the one v8 makes elsewhere: v7's omission is historical and unrepairable from here, and what v8 owes is that its own delta is complete, which it is. Since the repairLog is the artifact's audit instrument, a sentence inside it claiming a repair relationship that does not exist is worth correcting even though the underlying work is sound.
advisories.notBlocking: The completeness property I verified does not depend on this sentence; all 23 v7-to-v8 paths are named regardless of it.

advisories.title: The two fixture-corpus candidates are cited asymmetrically - v1 at a digest, v2 without one
advisories.detail: whatThisDoesNotDo[1] cites component-manifest-fixture-corpus.v1.json at d81a4ef9... but component-manifest-fixture-corpus.v2.json only as 'draft against this schema lineage'. The artifact's own citationDiscipline states that binding citations are '(path, digest-at-authoring, named property)'. I verified the v2 characterization is true and that v2 exists at e2781f449599909c7b2bfc8d827591911323f8633e2b5f419fcb27e772e6c9da, so nothing is wrong - but citing a moving draft without a digest is precisely the case where a digest matters most, and the repair that produced this clause was about preferring measured facts to unmeasured wording. A digest plus its reviewStatus would make the citation as precise as v1's.
advisories.notBlocking: No false claim; the non-acceptance disclaimer covers both candidates equally.

attackListDisposition.detail: My recursive diff found 23 changed/added/removed paths and every one is named: META-v8 covers /artifact, /version, /basedOn (predecessor, sha256, method), /appliesFindingsOf (the two v6 records removed, the two v7 records added, standing), /reviewGuidance and its new item, and the ADD of /openDecisions; V7-A2 covers /appliesFindingsOf/notFoldedThisSuccessor[0]; V7-S1 covers /sources/reMeasurementAtV2 and /sources/reMeasurementAtV5; V7-B1 covers /sources/reMeasurementAtV8; V7-A1 covers /whatThisDoesNotDo/1; the five repairLog appends are self-accounting. repairLog[0:50] is byte-identical to v7's complete log, so no landed repair was rewritten. The new top-level key /openDecisions is explicitly named by META-v8's fourth operation.

v1 exists at the cited digest d81a4ef9... (re-measured); 'independently REJECTED' holds for both independent reviews of it; v2 exists and is a draft whose own schemaContract pins this very subject at 22c9fbad..., so 'draft against this schema lineage' is accurate. This is a strict improvement over v6's false 'no fixture exists yet' and v7's unmeasured 'may exist'.

I extracted the parenthesised roster programmatically: V7-B1, V7-S1, V7-A1, V7-A2, META-v8 - a five-for-five match against the appended entries, in order, no phantom and no omission. The closing sentence 'The roster is closed; a later finding requires a new successor, not an in-place fold' is retained.

attackListDisposition.detail: I read both v7 verdicts and enumerated their ids. Codex v7: REJECT, blockers [V7-B1], shouldFix [], advisories [] - v8's codexV7 record states precisely that and reproduces Codex's title. Claude 2 v7: REJECT, blockers [], shouldFix [V7-S1], advisories [V7-A1, V7-A2] - v8's claude2V7 record states precisely that, and I confirm as its author. Every repairLog entry corresponds to a finding present in a named verdict file; no invented finding, and no v7 finding left unaddressed.

Predecessor v7 and both v7 verdict files re-measured and matching, including my own v7 verdict at aeb0e25b..., confirming the bytes folded are the bytes I filed. v8 parses under a duplicate-key-rejecting pairs hook with 0 duplicate keys.

whatIVerified.sourcePins: I re-measured every pin rather than trusting reMeasurementAtV8. All its claims are true: SRC-08, SRC-D and SRC-FRZ live digests are unchanged from reMeasurementAtV7 exactly as stated, and SRC-02 and SRC-03 still match their recorded v2 hashes. bindingSources, citationDiscipline, reMeasurementAtV6 and reMeasurementAtV7 are all byte-identical to v7.

whatIVerified.carriedContent: manifestSchema, indexSchema, lockSchema, rejectionRules, testCorpusRequirements, identityDependencies, namedOpenDecisions, namedDifferencesFromPrototype and measuredPrototypeBaselines all verified byte-identical to v7 as whole subtrees.

whatIDidNotCheck: I did not re-review v2 through v7 on their merits beyond confirming repairLog[0:50] is byte-identical and the named invariants are unchanged as whole subtrees.

I did not review either fixture-corpus candidate's contents. I measured v1's digest, read the verdict field of its two independent reviews, and read v2's header fields, solely to test v8's empirical claims. I express no view here on either candidate's quality or standing.
I did not evaluate DR-111's constraint or compatibility semantics, DR-112's ceremony, or the canonical-JSON profile. I confirmed only that v8 leaves them deferred exactly as v7 did.
I did not verify each named property of the moved SRC-08 / SRC-D / SRC-FRZ documents against their v2 bytes; I verified the live digests match v8's record.
I did not read the other current v8 reviewer's file.
I did not assess DR-103's register status and express no view on it. I did not edit file 08 or COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md.
This verdict is about the artifact's internal consistency and its handling of both v7 verdicts. It is not a statement that DR-103's acceptance-evidence cell is discharged.
